react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of eleven differentially abundant metabolites identified a dominant and statistically overwhelming enrichment in steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. Three independent methods—RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 5.8×10⁻¹⁸), mummichog empirical network analysis (p=0.000168), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p=5.77×10⁻⁷)—all converged on this pathway as the top hit, achieving cross-paradigm consensus with rank-1 status in each method. Six steroids drove this signal: dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), 17β-estradiol (KEGG:C00951), estrone (KEGG:C00468), androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), and dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917). In the RaMP ORA these six compounds achieved a fold enrichment of 1501-fold against SMPDB:SMP00068 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' and 2815-fold against WP:WP496 'Steroid biosynthesis'. The Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently recovered all six steroids plus structurally related C21 intermediates (15 total hits) within MUMM:C21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism. MetaboAnalystR KEGG confirmed hsa00140 'Steroid hormone biosynthesis' with p=5.77×10⁻⁷. Metabolite caffeine (KEGG:C07481) showed a secondary, weaker association with hsa00232 'Caffeine metabolism' (p=0.049). The steroid signal is biologically coherent: all six driver metabolites occupy sequential positions in the androgen→estrogen conversion axis, consistent with altered aromatase or 17β-HSD activity in the treatment condition. Sucrose (KEGG:C00089) appeared in sugar metabolism pathways but with marginal significance.
